Next year might see the largest iPhone display ever, according to a source with a decent track record of leaks.

Supply chain information suggests Apple is testing a new display that could be used in a new iPhone whose name remains unclear...

Naming mystery for next year's flagship iPhone

2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, and the market has long believed Apple is brewing something special. It is expected that this year will be the one when Apple comes very close to realising the long-held design vision for the iPhone — "a single sheet of glass".

Some speculate that Apple may launch a standalone 20th-anniversary edition iPhone, similar to the iPhone X of its time. However, more recent reports suggest this brand-new design will be released directly as next year's Pro models, namely the iPhone 19 Pro and Pro Max.

A third possibility is that, to mark the anniversary, Apple could jump straight from the iPhone 18 to the iPhone 20.

The largest iPhone display ever

Leaker "Digital Chat Station" (DCS) says supply chain information indicates Apple is testing the largest iPhone display to date. However, compared with the current 6.9-inch iPhone 17 Pro Max, the size increase is relatively modest.

In other words, they believe Apple will use a 7-inch display as a selling point.

DCS has no information on the actual purpose of this new display — if Apple really adopts it — but speculates it could be used in next year's iPhone Pro Max, though what it ends up being called remains unknown.

9to5Mac's take

Apple tests many different things, but most never make it to market, so even if this display really does appear in prototype form within the company's supply chain, it doesn't necessarily mean it will end up on an iPhone.

Nonetheless, if Apple's goal is to achieve that "single sheet of glass" look, being able to boast the largest display ever seems like a reasonable design element.
